label: the wrench (models/v_crowbar.mdl, models/p_crowbar.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl): a pipe wrench: red-painted handle worn to bare iron, a heavy toothed jaw

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_satchel.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, A, C, C where the asset was D, B, D, A: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's words, the head is a square block (sides.png: LEFT, RIGHT and TOP show a rectangular box at one end), not a pipe wrench's jaw. The red handle is a thin bar running into it. The outline reads as a hammer or a block on a stick, not a wrench.

M2.reason: Measured size is 18 long, 9.4 wide and 9.6 high, with the length within 0.001 of the 18 asked. Width and height are not asked for, so they are not held to a size.

M3.reason: The handle and the head are both there. The brief's named toothed jaw is a plain block with no teeth or V-jaw in any side view (sides.png: LEFT, FRONT-LEFT, BELOW). Teeth alone are not charged, since none of the line-up's Valve weapons shows them, but the jaw's form is wrong, so this is a shape fault. The head reads as a hammer-like block, not a jaw.

M4.reason: The handle is painted red and the bare tail end is steel grey, as the brief asks; the head is iron grey with the green-grey tint of the rest of the scene. Each region reads as the right material, with no colour out of place in sides.png, lineup.png or in-hand.png.

M5.reason: The steel has a grainy texture and the head's face carries a stippled pattern, but the worn-to-iron wear the brief asks for shows only as one grey cap on the handle (first-person.png). Nothing shows the rim or edges worn through.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test: the asset (D in lineup.png) was never picked as the one not made by Valve across four readings (picks C, A, C, C), so it passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The brief names no front or resting pose, and the views do not settle one. The head sits low and the handle rises from it in first-person.png, so it is not clear the model stands or lies on its origin the way the brief's crowbar-style w_ model does.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. At 92 triangles it is well under twice the weapons' median of 142, and under the third quartile of 187. No face is open, inside out, or floating in the views (sides.png). The stippled patch on the head's face reads as surface texture, not a hole.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the wrench stands upright in the middle of the view, head down and handle up, where the game's crowbar sits diagonally at the right edge with its hook up. It is not held the same way or the same way round. In attack.png the weapon's parts stay together through the swing, so nothing parts from the hands that are visible.
